categories.name: PWM Timer and PA8 Output Driver

criteria.criterion: After power-up or reset, PWM generation is present on Arduino D7/PA8 without any user interaction.
criteria.observable: Oscilloscope or logic-analyzer waveform on Arduino D7 / PA8 after reset
preconditions: NUCLEO-C5A3ZG is powered and connected to the measurement instrument.
The firmware image under test is programmed onto the board.
No user input is applied after reset.
procedure: Power-cycle or reset the board.
Begin observing Arduino D7 / PA8 before initialization completes.
Continue observing after board initialization completes.
criteria.expected: A periodic PWM waveform is present on D7/PA8 without user interaction.

criteria.criterion: A periodic PWM waveform is measurable at the electrically connected Arduino D7, CN9 pin 8, and MCU PA8 signal.
criteria.observable: Periodic voltage waveform measured at Arduino D7 / CN9 pin 8
preconditions: The board is powered and firmware initialization has completed.
The measurement instrument is connected to CN9 pin 8 referenced to board ground.
procedure: Run the firmware.
Probe CN9 pin 8 / Arduino D7 with an oscilloscope or logic analyzer.
Record the resulting signal.
criteria.expected: A periodic PWM waveform is measurable at D7/CN9 pin 8, corresponding to PA8.

criteria.criterion: The GPIO configuration assigns PA8 to the timer channel alternate function used by the PWM driver.
criteria.observable: PA8 GPIO alternate-function configuration in source or register initialization
preconditions: The firmware source and target configuration are available for review.
procedure: Inspect the PA8 GPIO initialization.
Identify the selected alternate-function value and timer channel.
Compare that assignment with the timer PWM channel used by the driver.
criteria.expected: PA8 is configured for the supported timer PWM alternate function, and the selected timer channel is the channel driven by the PWM implementation.

criteria.criterion: The measured PWM frequency is unchanged while the commanded duty cycle is ramped through its supported values.
criteria.observable: Frequency measurements from D7/PA8 at multiple commanded duty cycles
preconditions: PWM is active on D7/PA8.
The firmware exposes a way to command multiple duty-cycle values.
The frequency measurement instrument is connected to D7/PA8.
procedure: Measure the PWM frequency at an initial duty cycle.
Command successive duty-cycle values across the supported range.
Measure the frequency at each duty-cycle value.
criteria.expected: Every duty-cycle measurement reports the same carrier frequency as the initial measurement; no frequency change is observed during the ramp.

criteria.criterion: The startup PWM carrier frequency with the default configuration measures 1000 Hz.
criteria.observable: Frequency measurement of the startup waveform on D7/PA8
preconditions: The firmware is running with its default PWM configuration.
The board has completed initialization.
An oscilloscope or logic analyzer is connected to D7/PA8.
procedure: Reset or power-cycle the board without changing the PWM configuration.
Wait for PWM startup.
Measure the period or frequency of the D7/PA8 waveform.
criteria.expected: The measured carrier frequency is approximately 1000 Hz.

criteria.criterion: The PA8/D7 output is configured and documented as a 3.3 V logic GPIO signal rather than a variable 5 V supply rail.
criteria.observable: Schematic, board pinout, GPIO configuration, and interface documentation for PA8/D7
preconditions: The board schematic, pinout, firmware GPIO configuration, and test connection information are available.
procedure: Inspect the PA8/D7 electrical assignment and GPIO configuration.
Inspect the documented output voltage level and test connection guidance.
Check that the interface is identified as a logic output and not a supply rail.
criteria.expected: The reviewed interface identifies D7/PA8 as a 3.3 V logic output and does not specify it as a variable 5 V supply rail.

criteria.criterion: The external test connection requirements limit loads connected directly to D7/PA8 to the MCU GPIO electrical limits.
criteria.observable: Test fixture schematic, connection instructions, and stated GPIO voltage/current limits
preconditions: The external test fixture and MCU GPIO electrical specifications are available for review.
procedure: Inspect every direct external connection to D7/PA8 in the test fixture.
Compare the connected load and voltage/current requirements with the MCU GPIO limits.
Check that high-power loads are not specified for direct connection.
criteria.expected: All direct test loads are within the MCU GPIO electrical limits, and no high-power load is connected directly to D7/PA8.

criteria.criterion: During startup, D7/PA8 remains at one constant inactive logic level with no pulses until PWM is enabled.
criteria.observable: D7/PA8 logic level and pulse capture from reset through PWM enable
preconditions: The board is powered or reset with firmware initialization in progress.
The oscilloscope or logic analyzer is connected before reset or power-up.
procedure: Start waveform capture before powering up or resetting the board.
Observe D7/PA8 throughout GPIO and timer initialization.
Identify the instant PWM is enabled and inspect the preceding waveform.
criteria.expected: D7/PA8 remains at a single inactive logic level and contains no pulses before PWM enable.

criteria.criterion: The first active PWM period after enable has a commanded duty cycle of 0%.
criteria.observable: High-time of the first PWM period after enable on D7/PA8
preconditions: Startup capture includes the PWM-enable transition.
The firmware's initial commanded duty-cycle value is available to the test.
procedure: Capture D7/PA8 across the transition from inactive startup to PWM enable.
Locate the first complete PWM period after enable.
Measure its high-time.
criteria.expected: The first active PWM period has 0% high-time, so the output remains low for the entire period.

criteria.criterion: Every detected PWM/timer or PA8 configuration error routes initialization to an error path that leaves PA8 in the defined inactive state and does not enable PWM.
criteria.observable: Initialization error branches, GPIO state assignment, timer-enable call sequence, and failure reporting in source
preconditions: A negative-test build or fault-injection configuration that causes PWM/timer or PA8 initialization to fail is available for review.
procedure: Inspect each failure branch for timer, PWM, and PA8 configuration.
Trace the PA8 state assignment on the failure path.
Verify whether any timer/PWM enable operation or output-drive operation follows the failure.
Inspect the associated failure reporting path.
criteria.expected: On every configuration failure path, PA8 is assigned the defined inactive state, PWM is not enabled, and the failure is reported through the available build or test log mechanism.

criteria.criterion: At a commanded 50% duty cycle, the measured D7/PA8 high-time is approximately half of one PWM period.
criteria.observable: Measured high-time and period of the D7/PA8 waveform
preconditions: PWM is active at the configured carrier frequency.
The firmware can command 50% duty cycle.
The measurement instrument is connected to D7/PA8.
procedure: Command 50% duty cycle.
Capture several complete PWM periods.
Measure the high-time and total period for a representative period.
criteria.expected: The high-time is approximately 50% of the measured PWM period.

criteria.criterion: At a commanded 0% duty cycle, D7/PA8 remains continuously low, and at a commanded 100% duty cycle it remains continuously high.
criteria.observable: D7/PA8 logic level during commanded 0% and 100% duty-cycle intervals
preconditions: PWM is active and the firmware can command 0% and 100% duty cycle.
The measurement instrument is connected to D7/PA8.
procedure: Command 0% duty cycle and observe the output for multiple nominal PWM periods.
Command 100% duty cycle and observe the output for multiple nominal PWM periods.
criteria.expected: The output is continuously low at 0% duty and continuously high at 100% duty, with no transitions during either interval.

criteria.criterion: The PWM carrier-frequency override cannot be tested because the requirement does not identify the override mechanism or its supported frequency range.
criteria.blocked_reason: No named configuration/API/interface is provided for selecting the override frequency, and no supported override range or concrete non-default test value is specified.

criteria.criterion: At the start of each 10-second PWM cycle, the measured duty cycle on D7/PA8 is approximately 0%.
criteria.observable: Measured PWM duty cycle on Arduino D7/PA8 at each detected cycle start
preconditions: The PWM output is connected to a duty-cycle measurement instrument.
The firmware is running continuously.
procedure: Start duty-cycle capture on D7/PA8.
Identify the beginning of a PWM cycle.
Record the measured duty cycle at t = 0 s.
Repeat for multiple cycle starts.
criteria.expected: Approximately 0% at every cycle start.

criteria.criterion: The measured duty cycle rises monotonically from approximately 0% to approximately 100% and reaches approximately 100% at about 5.0 seconds.
criteria.observable: Time-stamped duty-cycle trace on Arduino D7/PA8 during the rising ramp
preconditions: The PWM output is connected to an oscilloscope, logic analyzer, or equivalent duty-cycle measurement instrument.
A rising ramp has just begun.
procedure: Capture the duty-cycle waveform from the start of a rising ramp through t = 5.0 s.
Calculate or inspect duty-cycle values at successive samples.
Record the time at which the duty cycle reaches approximately 100%.
criteria.expected: Duty-cycle samples never decrease during the rising ramp, and the duty cycle reaches approximately 100% at about 5.0 s.

criteria.criterion: The measured duty cycle falls monotonically from approximately 100% to approximately 0% over about 5.0 seconds and is approximately 0% at about 10.0 seconds from cycle start.
criteria.observable: Time-stamped duty-cycle trace on Arduino D7/PA8 during the falling ramp
preconditions: The PWM output is connected to a duty-cycle measurement instrument.
A complete rising ramp has reached approximately 100%.
procedure: Capture the duty-cycle waveform from the beginning of the falling ramp through t = 10.0 s from cycle start.
Calculate or inspect duty-cycle values at successive samples.
Record the duty cycle and elapsed time at the end of the falling ramp.
criteria.expected: Duty-cycle samples never increase during the falling ramp, the fall lasts about 5.0 s, and the endpoint is approximately 0% at about 10.0 s from cycle start.

criteria.criterion: The measured time from approximately 0% at one cycle start to approximately 0% at the next cycle end is approximately 10.0 seconds.
criteria.observable: Elapsed time between successive 0% cycle-start/end events on the PWM duty-cycle trace
preconditions: The PWM output is connected to a duty-cycle measurement instrument.
The firmware is running without reset or power interruption.
procedure: Capture at least two complete PWM cycles.
Timestamp each approximately 0% cycle-start event and the corresponding approximately 0% cycle-end event.
Subtract the start timestamp from the end timestamp.
criteria.expected: Each complete rise-and-fall cycle measures approximately 10.0 s.

criteria.criterion: The PWM ramp produces multiple consecutive 10-second cycles without terminating before a reset or power-off event.
criteria.observable: Continuous PWM duty-cycle capture showing successive rise-and-fall cycles
preconditions: The PWM output is connected to a duty-cycle measurement instrument.
The board has stable power and has not been reset.
procedure: Start a continuous capture.
Observe at least three consecutive complete rise-and-fall cycles.
Do not apply reset or power-off during the observation interval.
Then apply reset or power-off and stop the capture.
criteria.expected: At least three consecutive cycles are present with no termination before the reset or power-off event.

criteria.criterion: After a system reset, the PWM output returns to approximately 0% at the reset-start of the sequence and resumes the 10-second ramp.
criteria.observable: Measured PWM duty cycle and subsequent duty-cycle trace after reset
preconditions: The PWM output is connected to a duty-cycle measurement instrument.
The firmware is running before reset.
procedure: Apply a system reset to the board.
Capture the PWM output immediately after reset and for at least one complete cycle.
Record the initial duty cycle and verify the subsequent rise-and-fall sequence.
criteria.expected: The post-reset initial duty cycle is approximately 0%, followed by the defined 10-second ramp sequence.

criteria.criterion: During both ramp directions, sampled duty-cycle values are proportional to elapsed ramp time, including approximately 50% duty at 2.5 seconds into the rising ramp and 7.5 seconds from cycle start.
criteria.observable: Duty-cycle samples paired with timestamps during one complete cycle
preconditions: The PWM output is connected to a time-capable duty-cycle measurement instrument.
A complete 10-second cycle is captured from its 0% start.
procedure: Capture duty-cycle values with timestamps from t = 0 s through t = 10 s.
Compare samples against the linear 0%-to-100%-to-0% trajectory.
Inspect the values at t = 2.5 s and t = 7.5 s.
criteria.expected: The rising and falling samples follow proportional linear progress, with approximately 50% duty at both t = 2.5 s and t = 7.5 s.

criteria.criterion: The measured PWM duty-cycle trace reaches an approximately 0% endpoint at the start and end of each cycle.
criteria.observable: Minimum duty-cycle values in repeated PWM cycle captures
preconditions: The PWM output is connected to a duty-cycle measurement instrument.
At least one complete cycle is captured.
procedure: Capture multiple complete PWM cycles.
Record the minimum duty-cycle value at each cycle start and end.
criteria.expected: The start and end endpoints are approximately 0%.

criteria.criterion: The measured PWM duty-cycle trace reaches an approximately 100% endpoint at the end of each rising ramp.
criteria.observable: Maximum duty-cycle values in repeated PWM cycle captures
preconditions: The PWM output is connected to a duty-cycle measurement instrument.
At least one complete cycle is captured.
procedure: Capture multiple complete PWM cycles.
Record the maximum duty-cycle value during each rising ramp.
criteria.expected: The rising-ramp maximum is approximately 100% in every captured cycle.

criteria.criterion: Across all PWM updates, the measured output duty cycle remains within the inclusive range from 0% to 100%.
criteria.observable: Minimum and maximum measured duty-cycle values on D7/PA8 over repeated cycles
preconditions: The PWM output is connected to a duty-cycle measurement instrument.
The firmware runs through multiple cycles, including endpoint transitions.
procedure: Capture the PWM output over multiple complete cycles.
Determine the minimum and maximum measured duty-cycle values.
Compare both values with the inclusive bounds.
criteria.expected: Minimum duty cycle is at least 0% and maximum duty cycle is at most 100%.

criteria.criterion: An injected duty-cycle command below 0% produces 0% output and an injected command above 100% produces 100% output.
criteria.observable: Measured PWM duty cycle on D7/PA8 after below-range and above-range command injection
preconditions: The firmware exposes or permits a test injection point for duty-cycle commands.
The PWM output is connected to a duty-cycle measurement instrument.
procedure: Inject a duty-cycle command below 0%.
Measure the resulting PWM duty cycle.
Inject a duty-cycle command above 100%.
Measure the resulting PWM duty cycle.
criteria.expected: The below-range command produces 0% output and the above-range command produces 100% output.

criteria.criterion: After the PWM reaches approximately 100%, the next duty-cycle update is decreasing rather than remaining at a plateau.
criteria.observable: Consecutive duty-cycle samples around the 100% endpoint
preconditions: The PWM output is connected to an oscilloscope, logic analyzer, or equivalent time-resolved duty-cycle instrument.
A rising ramp reaches approximately 100%.
procedure: Capture the duty-cycle trace at sufficient resolution around the 100% endpoint.
Identify the update that reaches approximately 100%.
Compare it with the immediately following duty-cycle update.
criteria.expected: The immediately following update is lower than the endpoint value, with no intentional plateau beyond the update interval.

criteria.criterion: After the PWM reaches approximately 0%, the next duty-cycle update is increasing rather than remaining at a plateau.
criteria.observable: Consecutive duty-cycle samples around the 0% endpoint
preconditions: The PWM output is connected to an oscilloscope, logic analyzer, or equivalent time-resolved duty-cycle instrument.
A falling ramp reaches approximately 0%.
procedure: Capture the duty-cycle trace at sufficient resolution around the 0% endpoint.
Identify the update that reaches approximately 0%.
Compare it with the immediately following duty-cycle update.
criteria.expected: The immediately following update is higher than the endpoint value, with no intentional plateau beyond the update interval.

criteria.criterion: The duty-cycle update path contains no blocking delay call or loop that waits for elapsed time before returning.
criteria.observable: Source code and call graph for the duty-cycle update routine
preconditions: The firmware source and duty-cycle update call path are available for review.
procedure: Locate the duty-cycle update routine and every function it calls synchronously.
Inspect the path for blocking delay APIs and polling loops that wait for time or an external event.
Record any such call or loop found in the update path.
criteria.expected: No blocking delay API or time-waiting polling loop is present in the duty-cycle update path.

criteria.criterion: Duty-cycle updates are scheduled by a timer, system tick, interrupt-driven callback, or equivalent mechanism that returns control to normal firmware execution between updates.
criteria.observable: Source code showing the update scheduler and duty-cycle update callback or state-machine transition
preconditions: The firmware source and scheduler configuration are available for review.
procedure: Identify how duty-cycle updates are triggered.
Trace one update invocation from the scheduler to the update logic.
Verify that the scheduler triggers discrete updates without waiting synchronously for the ramp to complete.
criteria.expected: The update path is driven by a timer, tick, interrupt callback, or equivalent non-blocking mechanism, and each update returns control before the next scheduled update.

criteria.criterion: The measured PWM duty cycle is approximately 50% at 2.5 s after the ramp starts.
criteria.observable: Oscilloscope duty-cycle measurement on the PWM output at PA8/Arduino D7, as wired on the target board
preconditions: The NUCLEO-C5A3ZG is running the firmware.
The PWM output is connected to the oscilloscope.
The ramp start event and time reference are observable or triggerable.
The project-defined meaning of the PA8 and Arduino D7 connection is known.
procedure: Connect the oscilloscope to the configured PWM output.
Trigger the time measurement at ramp start.
Measure duty cycle at 2.5 s.
Record the measured duty-cycle percentage.
criteria.expected: The measured duty cycle is approximately 50%, subject to the project's measurement tolerance.

criteria.criterion: The measured PWM duty cycle is approximately 50% at 7.5 s after the ramp starts.
criteria.observable: Oscilloscope duty-cycle measurement on the PWM output at PA8/Arduino D7, as wired on the target board
preconditions: The NUCLEO-C5A3ZG is running the firmware.
The PWM output is connected to the oscilloscope.
The ramp start event and time reference are observable or triggerable.
The project-defined meaning of the PA8 and Arduino D7 connection is known.
procedure: Connect the oscilloscope to the configured PWM output.
Trigger the time measurement at ramp start.
Measure duty cycle at 7.5 s.
Record the measured duty-cycle percentage.
criteria.expected: The measured duty cycle is approximately 50%, subject to the project's measurement tolerance.

criteria.criterion: The ramp waveform has no unexpected duty-cycle jumps or long pauses.
criteria.blocked_reason: The acceptance statement does not define the maximum allowed duty-cycle step, pause duration, update interval, or what constitutes an unexpected jump, so no reproducible pass/fail threshold can be asserted.

categories.name: External Load and USB Development Interface

criteria.criterion: The design and test setup show an external driver stage between every load exceeding the applicable MCU GPIO electrical limit and the MCU pin, with no direct high-power-load connection to the pin.
criteria.observable: Schematic, wiring, and test setup showing the connection path from Arduino D7 or PA8 to each external load
preconditions: Testing or usage involves external loads
The applicable GPIO maximum load limits from the MCU datasheet are available
procedure: Review the schematic and physical test setup for each external load.
Compare each load's electrical requirements with the applicable GPIO limits.
Verify that every load exceeding those limits is connected through an external driver stage.
criteria.expected: For every load exceeding a GPIO limit, an external driver stage is present in the signal path; zero such loads are connected directly to Arduino D7, PA8, or another MCU GPIO.

criteria.criterion: During development and verification, the board receives power through USB and the programming/debug connection is established through USB.
criteria.observable: USB connection, board power indication, and programming/debug tool connection or session
preconditions: Development or verification activity is in progress
A suitable USB cable and host computer are available
procedure: Connect the board to the development host using USB.
Verify that the board powers up from the USB connection.
Program the board and establish the debug interface using the USB connection.
criteria.expected: The board is powered by USB, and both programming and debugging are performed through the USB connection during the test run.
